title: 11wdrg4
The Bay'a and the Camel
hook: When the people ran to Imam Ali, he took up the heavy caliphate knowingly. His resolve for justice gave birth to the Camel.
scenes.0.text: When Caliph Uthman was killed in Medina in Dhu al-Hijja 35 H, the city fell into turmoil. The Ansar and the Muhajirun ran to **Imam Ali** at the Prophet's Mosque. He took up this heavy duty knowingly. Bay'a is a pledge of allegiance. The bay'a was taken there. The state he inherited was troubled. The mistakes left over from the period of the caliphs before him, injustices, nepotism, wrongly distributed properties and corrupt governors were there. His first task was to establish justice. He began to take back the wrongly distributed properties to the bayt al-mal, that is, the common treasury. He dismissed the corrupt governors. This resolve for justice gave rise to the opposition at the Camel and at Siffin.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.1.text: In Medina, Talha and al-Zubayr also pledged allegiance to **Imam Ali**. Imam Ali began to replace Caliph Uthman's governors and to draw the wrongly distributed properties into the bayt al-mal. In Syria, **Mu'awiya** stayed in his place. Some of those who pledged allegiance had not given this word from the heart. They would base their objections on the dismissal of the governors and the taking back of property. This objection would turn into an army at the Camel and into **Mu'awiya**'s resistance at Siffin.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: s20l3t
Talha
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: 52j0kp
Al-Zubayr
scenes.1.art.actors.2.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.2.text: **Mu'awiya**, the governor of Syria, announced that he would not pledge allegiance to **Imam Ali** until Caliph Uthman's blood was avenged. Uthman's blood was a pretext for him. What he really wanted was power. **Imam Ali**, however, wanted first to establish order and then leave the case to the court. He was not after hasty revenge.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.3.text: Aisha, Talha and al-Zubayr, who were in Mecca for the umra, cited Caliph Uthman's blood as their justification. They set out for Basra. They marched an army against **Imam Ali**, to whom they had pledged allegiance. They reopened for debate his right that had only just been accepted.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: rrckkf
Aisha
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: s20l3t
Talha
scenes.3.art.actors.2.label: 52j0kp
Al-Zubayr
scenes.4.text: The army going from Mecca to Basra reached the water of Haw'ab at night. Haw'ab is the name of a water on the Basra road. Dogs barked. Aisha asked, "What water is this?" They said, "Haw'ab." She remembered the warning the Prophet had spoken to his wives: "How will it be with you when the dogs of Haw'ab bark at one of you?" She wanted to turn back. Those with Talha and al-Zubayr made her continue on the way. According to the report, false witnesses were brought and made to say, "This is not Haw'ab." Aisha was made to march on regardless. In Basra a clash broke out with the governor Uthman b. Hunayf.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: rrckkf
Aisha
scenes.5.text: **Imam Ali** set out from Kufa. He sent an envoy to prevent war. Before the battle began he called al-Zubayr. Years earlier, when the Prophet saw the two together, he had asked al-Zubayr: "Do you love him?" Al-Zubayr had said, "Yes. What reason is there for me not to love him?" And the Prophet had said, "But one day you will oppose him and fight him, wronging him." Imam Ali recalled this saying point by point. Al-Zubayr said, "I had forgotten." He said he would not enter the battle. He spurred his horse. He broke through the ranks and left the battlefield. After he left he was killed.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: 52j0kp
Al-Zubayr
scenes.6.text: When peace was not enough, the two armies met. The other side had declared war on **Imam Ali**. The camel Aisha rode was the place where the other side gathered. The fighting went on around that camel. When the camel collapsed, there was no gathering place left. TDV's entry on the Camel writes that the camel was hamstrung by Imam Ali's order and that about seventy people died around the howdah. The army dispersed. This is why the battle ended. It was not some spontaneous spell. Talha was killed in the battle. Al-Zubayr, however, had been killed after leaving the field. **Imam Ali** had not wanted blood to be shed. Even so, blood was shed.
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: rrckkf
Aisha
scenes.6.art.actors.2.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.7.text: After the battle, **Imam Ali** released the prisoners. He did not apply the ruling of spoils over property, women and children. He hosted Aisha with respect. He sent her off to Medina with her brother Muhammad b. Abi Bakr. Though victorious, he did not take revenge. The side that is in the right behaves like this.
scenes.7.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: rrckkf
Aisha
scenes.7.art.actors.2.label: yenjdy
Muhammad b. Abi Bakr
scenes.8.text: After the Camel, it is narrated that Aisha was grieved. **The Camel** is the day on which **Imam Ali** stood closer to the truth. He chose patience toward those who broke the pledge of allegiance. Even so, he did not give up the right. The turn would come to **Mu'awiya**, waiting in Syria.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: rrckkf
Aisha
sunni.0.says: The bay'a to Imam Ali, Mu'awiya's stance, the setting out for Basra, the Battle of the Camel and its aftermath; the report of the reminder to al-Zubayr is also transmitted.
sunni.1.says: The account of how the bay'a was taken and of the process leading to the Camel.
sunni.2.says: The course of the Battle of the Camel.
sunni.3.says: Reports about Aisha and the events; reports narrating that Aisha regretted are transmitted in this source and in works such as Ibn Abi Shayba, al-Dhahabi and al-Hakim.
sunni.4.says: Aisha reaches the waters of Banu Amir at night. Dogs bark. She asks the name of the water. When told Haw'ab, she wants to turn back. Those with her, al-Zubayr among them, tell her to go on. She remembers the Prophet's saying, "How will it be with you when the dogs of Haw'ab bark at one of you?"
sunni.4.grade: The text was read in the Musnad under these numbers
sunni.5.says: No. 5573: Imam Ali reminds al-Zubayr that, while they were together in the shade of one of the Ansar, the Prophet asked "Do you love him?", that al-Zubayr said yes, and that he said, "You will oppose him and fight him, wronging him." Al-Zubayr turns back. No. 5574: "You will fight him and you will be the one who wrongs him." Al-Zubayr says he had forgotten and leaves. Al-Hakim says this report is sahih. No. 5575: Al-Zubayr tells the hadith to his son Abdullah and leaves, breaking through the ranks.
sunni.6.says: He says Imam Ali was in the right at the Camel; he calls it an error of ijtihad for Talha, al-Zubayr and Aisha. This report is taken from the literature and has not been verified from a primary text.
sunni.7.says: The view that Imam Ali was in the right at the Camel and that the other side erred is attributed to him; the rules of fighting rebels are derived from Imam Ali's practice at the Camel. Unverified report.
sunni.8.says: The rulings on fighting rebels (not killing the wounded, not pursuing those who flee, not counting property as spoils) are derived from Imam Ali's conduct at the Camel and at Siffin. Unverified report.
shia.0.says: Imam Ali's conditions for accepting the caliphate and his sermon upon the insistence on the bay'a. There is debate over the attribution of the sermons.
shia.1.says: Aisha's wanting to turn back at Haw'ab, the saying "This is not Haw'ab" with false witnesses, and the Prophet's saying being recalled to al-Zubayr and his leaving the battlefield. The page number was not given separately.
shia.2.says: The first correspondence between Imam Ali and Mu'awiya. In Sunni rijal criticism Nasr is counted as an "extreme Shia," but in terms of material he is an early source.
shia.3.says: The general course of events. He is considered a historian with Shia leanings.
disputes.0.title: uex6wm
Caliph Uthman's blood: order first, or retribution first?
disputes.0.sunni: Caliph Uthman's blood has been discussed on both sides. The Sunni view understands both Imam Ali's reasoning and the stance of the other side as an ijtihad.
disputes.0.shia: Caliph Uthman's blood has been discussed on both sides. In the Shia account, Imam Ali wanted first to establish order and leave the case to the judiciary, and opposition to this is not seen as legitimate.
disputes.1.title: az03t4
Was the bay'a of Talha and al-Zubayr from the heart?
disputes.1.sunni: That Talha and al-Zubayr pledged allegiance is common ground in the sources. Whether this bay'a was given voluntarily or under pressure is separately reported.
disputes.1.shia: That Talha and al-Zubayr pledged allegiance is common ground in the sources. Imam Ali maintained that this bay'a was given from the heart and did not accept the later claim that it was given under compulsion.
disputes.2.title: 1qoyfta
What was Aisha's grief about?
disputes.2.sunni: Reports narrating that Aisha was grieved are found in the sources. The chain of each report and the subject of the grief are separately debated.
disputes.2.shia: Reports narrating that Aisha was grieved are found in the sources. In the Shia account, her opposition to Imam Ali is seen as a wrong step.
questions.0: Imam Ali took up the caliphate knowingly. How does his taking back wrongful properties and dismissing corrupt governors describe to you the opposition against him at the Camel and Siffin?
questions.1: When Imam Ali reminded al-Zubayr of the Prophet's question "Do you love him?" and the saying "you will fight him, wronging him," al-Zubayr left the ranks. What does this scene tell you about the meaning of standing with Imam Ali?
questions.2: After the battle Imam Ali released the prisoners and sent Aisha off to Medina with respect. What does this courtesy make you think about his intention?
questions.3: Many Sunni scholars find Imam Ali closer to the truth at the Camel. Does this shared view open a door for you to know him more closely?
summary: After Caliph Uthman was killed, Imam Ali took up the caliphate knowingly. At Haw'ab Aisha wanted to turn back, yet was made to march on. Imam Ali reminded al-Zubayr of the Prophet's saying. Al-Zubayr left the ranks and was later killed. Imam Ali pardoned the prisoners and sent Aisha off to Medina with respect.
key: The first civil war against Imam Ali
notes.0: After Caliph Uthman was killed, Imam Ali took up the caliphate knowingly.
notes.1: Talha, al-Zubayr and Aisha cited Caliph Uthman's blood as justification and turned toward Basra.
notes.2: Mu'awiya, too, announced that he would not pledge allegiance until Caliph Uthman's blood was avenged.
notes.3: At the Camel, when the Prophet's saying was recalled to him, al-Zubayr left the battlefield and was later killed. Talha was killed in the battle.
notes.4: After the battle, Imam Ali released the prisoners and sent Aisha off to Medina with respect.
